edges.description: Loss of IRX5 impairs ventricular conduction programs by disrupting regulation of Nav1.5, Connexin 40, and SCN5A expression in cardiomyocytes.
Biallelic IRX5 homeodomain dysfunction affects embryonic brain development and manifests clinically with variable intellectual disability.
Neurodevelopmental dysfunction downstream of IRX5 deficiency can manifest with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
Craniofacial and auditory sensory developmental abnormalities downstream of IRX5 deficiency include sensorineural hearing impairment.
Ocular developmental abnormalities in IRX5 deficiency manifest with high myopia.
Disturbed craniofacial patterning from impaired neural crest and branchial arch progenitor migration manifests as severe hypertelorism.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Molecular Update on the Fourth Reported Family with Hamamy Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing studies performed on the 2 affected individuals and one obligate carrier revealed the presence of a homozygous c.503G>A (p.Arg168His) missense mutation in IRX5 in both sibs, not reported in any other family.
